text: Performance Analytics — PA for short — is ServiceNow's more advanced analytics product, and it exists to answer a question that a standard report structurally cannot answer.

A report, from the last lesson, runs a live query the moment you open it. That makes it always current, but it also means it has no memory — ask it how today compares to last Tuesday, and it can't answer, because it only ever sees the table as it is right now. A report answers what does this look like right now. PA answers how has this changed over time. That's the entire reason PA exists as a separate layer on top of ordinary reporting.

PA makes trend possible through snapshots. A scheduled collector job runs, typically once a day, and captures a single number at that moment — number of open incidents, say — storing it permanently. A year of daily collector runs becomes 365 stored data points. A live report could never produce that history, because by the time you ran it again, today's exact count would already be gone.

PA has its own vocabulary. An Indicator is the KPI itself — number of open incidents, average time to resolve, SLA breach rate. A collector job snapshots that indicator on schedule. A Widget is how its history gets displayed — a trend line, a scorecard against a target — and widgets are what actually land on dashboards. And a Breakdown slices an indicator's history by a dimension, like priority or assignment group, so each slice gets its own trend line, not just a current count.

In many ServiceNow editions, PA is licensed separately from base reporting, and that reflects real additional engineering — scheduled collector jobs, a dedicated snapshot store, a KPI and target framework base reports simply don't have.
Right now versus over time — that's the line between a Report and PA. Next, building a dashboard: where reports and PA widgets actually live side by side.
